ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In Figure 2, point P on the equator and point Q on the meridian have equal noon solar altitudes; point P is located west of point O, and arc OP is equal to OQ. <image1> When location P is farthest west of location O, what is the longitude of location P?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a horizontal line is labeled as the equator, and a vertical line is labeled as the 20°E meridian; the intersection of the two lines is O. Point P is on the equator and to the left of point O, that is, west of point O; point Q is on the 20°E meridian and below point O, that is, south of point O. The problem also states that arc OP is equal to OQ. Reasoning: Let arc OP=OQ=x°. Since O is at the intersection of the 20°E meridian and the equator, P is on the equator and is x° west of O, so P's latitude is 0° and longitude is 20°E−x°. Q is on the 20°E meridian and is x° south of O, so Q's latitude is −x° and longitude is 20°E. The noon solar altitude formula is H=90°−|φ−δ|, where φ is the local latitude and δ is the latitude of the direct solar point. The noon solar altitudes of P and Q are equal, so 90°−|0−δ|=90°−|−x−δ|, that is, |δ|=|x+δ|. Since x>0, solving gives x=−2δ, so the direct solar point must be in the Southern Hemisphere. To make P located farthest west of O, that is, to make x maximum, the minimum solar declination δ=−23°26′ should be taken. Thus x=−2×(−23°26′)=46°52′. The longitude of location P=20°E−46°52′=26°52′W.

raw_record.question_text:
In Figure 2, point P on the equator and point Q on the meridian have equal noon solar altitudes; point P is located west of point O, and arc OP is equal to OQ.

<image1>

When location P is farthest west of location O, what is the longitude of location P?

method.method_draft: Let OP = OQ = x°. From the image, P has latitude 0° and longitude 20°E − x°, while Q is at latitude −x° and longitude 20°E. Equal noon solar altitude gives 90° − |0 − δ| = 90° − |−x − δ|, so |δ| = |x + δ|. For x > 0 this yields x = −2δ, meaning the Sun must be in the Southern Hemisphere. To make P farthest west, maximize x; this occurs at the minimum solar declination δ = −23°26′. Hence x = 46°52′, and P longitude = 20°E − 46°52′ = 26°52′W.

method.method_draft: Represent the common arc OP = OQ as x°. Then P is at latitude 0° and Q is at latitude x°S. Because their noon solar altitudes are equal, their latitude distances from the direct-sun latitude are equal; with P on the equator and Q south of it, the direct-sun latitude must be the midpoint between 0° and x°S, namely x/2°S. To place P as far west as possible, x must be as large as possible, so the midpoint/direct-sun latitude must be as far south as possible: 23°26′S. Thus x/2 = 23°26′, x = 46°52′. Starting from O at 20°E and moving 46°52′ west gives P at 26°52′W.
